 How DWTS Season 35 is playing out
 Frech has maintained his position atop the market through consistently strong performances alongside professional partner Daniella Karagach. He earned 36 out of 40 points during October 13's Super Bowl Night, reinforcing his status as the contestant to beat.
 Jenna Dewan also scored 36 points last week, matching Frech's judges' total. Their performances demonstrated that while the market strongly favors Frech, other contestants remain competitive on the dance floor.
 Guillermo Rodriguez and partner Witney Carson were eliminated following Super Bowl Night, further narrowing the field. As the season progresses, judges' scores and audience voting will become increasingly important in determining who survives each week.
 Dancing With the Stars: What to watch
 Tuesday's Dedication Night introduces another opportunity for contestants to deliver standout performances and potentially shift the Kalshi winner market.
 Frech's continued dominance: Despite his slight market decline, Frech remains comfortably ahead. Can another strong performance reinforce his position?
 Glenn's emotional routine: The Olympic figure skater and partner Pasha Pashkov will perform a contemporary dance dedicated to Glenn's sister, creating an opportunity for a memorable performance.
 Dewan's partner change: Dewan will dance with Alan Bersten while regular partner Val Chmerkovskiy serves a one-week suspension. How quickly can the new pairing establish chemistry?
 Higgins' pursuit: Higgins remains among the leading challengers, consistently delivering strong performances as the season progresses. She needs another standout performance to narrow Frech's advantage.
 Elimination uncertainty: With the field shrinking, contestants further down the leaderboard face increasing pressure to combine strong judges' scores with viewer support.
 The market remains heavily tilted toward Frech, but Dedication Night offers another chance for the chasing pack to make its case.
 Trading on Dancing With the Stars at Kalshi
 Kalshi offers Yes and No contracts on which contestant will officially win Season 35. Prices fluctuate as traders react to performances, eliminations, and changing expectations.
 For example, a Yes contract purchased for 53¢ pays $1 if Frech wins the competition, generating a 47¢ profit before fees. An incorrect contract typically settles at zero, resulting in the loss of the purchase price.
 Traders can also sell contracts before the winner is announced, subject to available liquidity and market prices. As with any prediction market , it's important to understand the contract terms, recognize the risk of loss, and trade only with money you can afford to lose.
